Commentary.Commentary: So, 197 is the final target. Sri Lanka will surely head into this as the favorites. History will be created if they manage to knock off these. On the other hand, South Africa will surely need early wickets if they want to defend this total. What will happen? The floodlights are on as well, due to the fading light. We will be back for the final innings of the game! Join us in ten minutes...

Finally, the innings has come to an end! I say finally because there were 3 chances for the last wicket to fall before it indeed fell at the end. What a brilliant comeback from Sri Lanka in this match. At 90/3, it looked like Du Plessis and Hashim Amla were taking this game away from them but the last 7 wickets have fallen for a meager 38 runs only! The lead has been restricted to under 200 and there is a real chance for 2-0 now! The post-Tea session began with South Africa at 91/5 and they would have looked to bat at least till the end of the day. That though has not happened as the last 5 wickets have fallen with just over an hour into the final session. Lakmal was inspired and picked up 4 wickets. Dhananjaya de Silva came to the party too with 3 wickets. Faf du Plessis on the batting front, got to his fifty but was stranded at the other end as his team was eventually bowled out.

OUT! Height does not save him this time as the ball is clipping the top of leg stump. That is the end of the South African innings. Four-fer for Lakmal but let us also credit the fielder who did not let the batsmen run two on the previous ball. That meant Olivier was on strike and he fails to negotiate the next ball. It is bowled on a length and around off, it comes back in a little. Duanne lunges and tries to defend. He misses and it hits his front pad. An appeal follows and the umpire raises his finger. Duanne has no option but to review and replays show that the on-field call is the right one. THE HOSTS HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 128! THE TARGET IS 197!

Review time... Third review in three overs! This time from South Africa. Olivier has been adjudged LBW here and it being the last wicket, he has gone upstairs after consulting his skipper at the other end. Can height save him once more?

Fifty for Faf du Plessis. The skipper leading from the front here. He kept losing partners at the other end but has played a very valuable knock. The hosts will hope he can add a few more. This is full and on the pads, Faf flicks it towards mid-wicket. The fielder there makes a good diving stop and he keeps it down to one. Good fielding effort that as it brings Olivier on strike.
The floodlights have been switched on...

NOT OUT! Faf is correct as Olivier has made it in. Lakmal has probably taken a little too much time to whip the bails off. It is on the pads, Faf flicks it through square leg. He takes one and goes for the second. The fielder there picks the ball up and throws it to the bowler. Lakmal collects it and dislodges the stumps. An appeal follows and the umpire takes it upstairs. Replays roll in and it shows Olivier's dive has saved him.
Is that the end of the innings? Faf looks confident that it is not a run out. Sri Lanka are confident that it is a run out. Who will be correct?
Yorker on middle, Olivier manages to keep it out towards mid-wicket.
FOUR! Floated on middle and leg, Olivier works it fine towards fine leg. The fielder chases it and slides to stop it but in vain. It was racing away to the boundary.
Short on off, du Plessis makes room and cuts it towards point for a run.
Flighted delivery on off, Olivier looks to defend but gets an outside edge. It goes towards third man. The batsmen cross ends.
Tossed up on middle, du Plessis tucks it towards mid-wicket for a run.

NOT OUT! Again, it is missing the stumps. This time, not due to the height but due to the turn the ball is seen to be missing leg stump. A flatter ball on middle, du Plessis looks to sweep and misses the ball. A loud appeal ensues and Aleem Dar, the umpire is unmoved. A long deliberation between the SL team and in the end, Karunaratne decides to go upstairs once more. There is no inside edge and though the ball was hitting him in line, the turn causes it to miss the leg stump. Both reviews have been lost now in the space of four balls. A lot of tension here but the innings will continue, yet again!
Another review for LBW! This seems to be missing leg comfortably. That is what the bowler is also thinking. But Dickwella reckons that it is worth taking...
Fuller one on middle, kept out by Duanne towards mid off.

NOT OUT! Yes, height is an issue. The Ball Tracker shows us that the ball is missing the stumps. A length ball on middle, Olivier steps ahead and looks to flick this away on the leg side but misses the ball and gets hit on the knee roll. There is a loud appeal and the umpire says not out. Sri Lanka go upstairs but the replays show that the ball is seen to be missing the stumps. The innings will go on yet again. Sri Lanka have only 1 review left now.
Review time... Loud appeal from Sri Lanka for an LBW. Olivier is struck in front but height seems to be an issue. Let's see what the replays have to say...
Bowls a yorker on off, Olivier somehow manages to dig it out.
On a good length on middle, Olivier defends it off the back foot.
On middle, Olivier keeps it out.
Good length delivery on middle, Olivier defends it to the on side.
Bowls this one down the leg side. Left alone by the batsman.

NO BALL! Madness here at Port Elizabeth! Du Plessis is stumped off a no ball. A flatter one outside off by Dhananjaya and it keeps low. Faf comes ahead and looks to smash it over mid off but misses the ball. The keeper collects and removes the bail. The umpire though wants to check the front foot. Lo and behold! Dhananjaya has overstepped. The innings will continue. Dhananjaya de Silva has his head in his shirt in shame, a no ball for a spinner. Unforgiveable!
Floated on off, Olivier looks to defend but gets an outside edge. It goes wide of first slip. It goes towards third man for a run.
Tossed up on off, Olivier defends it off the front foot.
Defended by Olivier on the front foot to a flatter ball outside off.
Duanne Olivier is the last man in.

OUT! What a brilliant catch! The ghosts of the first innings return all over again, South Africa have lost their way. From 90/3 to 116/9! A flatter ball on middle, Steyn comes ahead and looks to turn it away on the leg side but manages to hit it in the air and only as far as Thirimanne at short leg. Lahiru fails to grab it in the first attempt but manages to gobble it in the second. Sri Lanka have made a stunning comeback in this game!
Flatter one on middle, du Plessis manages to bring his bat down in time despite playing it on the back foot. Turns it away towards square leg for a single.
On a length and kept out by Steyn down the ground.
Goes full this time outside off, driven towards mid off by Steyn.
Bouncer to welcome Steyn. Dale ducks under that one and lets it go.
Dale Steyn walks in next, at number 10.

OUT! South Africa lose their eighth wicket. Lakmal gets his third and he has struck twice in two overs. Good length delivery outside off, Rabada looks to defend towards the off side but gets an outside edge. It almost went of the top of the bat of Rabada. It goes towards second slip where Kusal Mendis takes a comfortable catch. Poor Faf... running out of partners.
Full and outside off, du Plessis drives it through covers for a run.
A length ball just outside off, Du Plessis dabs it towards covers off the back foot.
Tossed up on off, Rabada looks to defend but misses it.
Floated on off, Rabada blocks it off the front foot.
Tossed up on off, Rabada keeps it out.
Flighted delivery on middle, Kagiso defends it off the back foot.
Floated on middle, Rabada defends it off the back foot.
Tossed up on middle, du Plessis flicks it towards the leg side for a run.
Again on a good length on off, Rabada blocks it well.
Good length delivery on off, Rabada defends it out.

OUT! LBW! That is as plumb as it gets. South Africa lose their 7th. Good length delivery on middle and leg, Maharaj looks to flick but misses it and gets hit on the pads. Lakmal appeals and the umpire raises his finger straightaway. Keshav has a word with his skipper but du Plessis is not too keen on taking it. Maharaj walks off. Looked plumb and Hawk Eye confirms, hitting the top of middle. Kagiso Rabada is the next batsman in. The Proteas are effectively 181/7.
On off, Maharaj keeps it out.
Now a short leg is in place!
Good length delivery on middle and leg, Maharaj looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads. The ball lobs onto the pitch. If short leg would have been there it would have been a catch.
A good length delivery outside off, Maharaj comes ahead and defends the ball towards the off side.
Floated on off, the skipper keeps it out.
Flighted delivery on off, Maharaj looks to defend but gets an outside edge. It goes towards third man. The fielder chases it and does well to stop it before the ropes. The batsmen get three runs.
Tossed up on off, Keshav blocks it off his front foot.
Floated on middle and leg, Maharaj sweeps it to square leg.
Flighted delivery on off, Maharaj keeps it out.
Tossed up on off, Maharaj plays it to covers.
On off, du Plessis blocks it off his back foot.
Good length delivery outside off, the skipper easily lets it go.
FOUR! Nice shot. Full on middle and leg, du Plessis flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
On off, du Plessis defends it off the back foot.
Good length delivery on off, du Plessis plays it towards mid off.
Fuller one outside off, Maharaj pats it towards mid on and picks up another risky single. This time though, the fielder fails to collect the ball cleanly.
A flatter one on middle, pushed away towards mid-wicket by Faf to end the over.
A quick and fuller one on middle, pushed by Maharaj towards the right of mid on for a single.
Shorter one outside off, Faf cuts it away through covers for a single.
Flatter one outside off, defended with soft hands by Du Plessis.

NOT OUT! Maharaj is just in by inches despite running at an angle! Tossed up on off, Maharaj drives it towards mid off and sets off for a quick single. Siriwardena, the substitute fielder at mid off picks up the ball cleanly and scores a direct hit at the bowler's end. It is referred upstairs and the replays show that the batsman was just in. It was touch and go eventually but the third umpire has ruled it in the favour of the batsman. Looked like the right decision. South Africa will be thankful and look to run safer runs now, as they can ill-afford run-outs, especially at this stage.
Run out appeal! A direct-hit from Siriwardena at mid off. Looked like Maharaj was inside the crease to the naked eye but he ran at an angle at the end. Can that cause any problems?
Floated on middle, du Plessis flicks it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Bowls a bumper, Maharaj does well to duck under it.
Outside off, Maharaj lets it go.
Length delivery on middle, du Plessis pushes it to mid on.
On off, the skipper keeps it out.
Good length delivery on off, du Plessis defends it off the back foot.
Length ball outside off, defended with soft hands towards the off side.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery. A wicket maiden from Dhananjaya.
Another flatter one on middle, Maharaj should have really been playing ahead to that one. In the end, just manages to get his bat down in time to prevent himself from being plumb in front.
A flatter ball outside off, defended with soft hands towards the off side.
Keshav Maharaj walks in at number 8.

OUT! Another edge! And taken beautifully by Mendis at first slip! Sri Lanka strike immediately after the break. Tossed up on off, Mulder comes forward, looks to defend but gets an outside edge. It goes straight into the bucket hands of Kusal Mendis who takes his second catch. The hosts have lost three wickets in the space of 10 runs. South Africa are in deep trouble now.
Floated on off, Mulder drives it back to the bowler.
Tossed up on off, Mulder defends it off the back foot.
Full on middle and leg, the skipper drives it to mid on.
Good length delivery on middle, du Plessis defends it off the front foot.
Full on middle, du Plessis plays it to mid off.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground. One run added to the total. 100 up for South Africa. The lead is now 168.
Length ball outside off, defended with soft hands on the off side.
Fuller length ball on middle, push-driven towards mid on.
On middle and leg, du Plessis plays it to mid on.
Flighted delivery on middle, Faf defends it off the back foot.
Floated on off, the skipper keeps it out.

FOUR! The outside edge goes to the other side of slip this time. Tossed up on off, du Plessis looks to turn it away on the leg side but closes the bat face a little too early. He gets an outside edge that flies quick and wide of first slip. It goes towards third man for a boundary. Second time lucky for Faf! The last time the ball took a really fine edge and it went to the left of that slip whereas this time the ball went square and away to the right of him. Talk about living a charmed life!
Full on middle, the skipper drives it to mid on.
Tossed up on off, du Plessis keeps it out.
Dhananjaya de Silva to bowl from the other end.
Kept out off a good length towards square leg.
FOUR! Lovely shot first ball! A fuller length ball on off and middle, Mulder presents the straight bat and pushes it wide of mid off for a boundary.

We are back for the final session which is going to be a long but one can expect it to be an exciting one. Faf du Plessis makes his way out to the middle. He walks out with Wiaan Mulder who is the new batsman. The latter will be on strike and he will face Lakmal who has two balls to go in this over.
... Day 2, Session 3 ...

The session began with the hosts starting at 10/1 but they soon slipped to 51/3 as they lost both Markram and Bavuma. Then came the decent stand between Hashim and Faf. Just when it looked like the match was going into the Tea break with the home team only 3 down and the happier one, the tide has turned again. Sri Lanka have come back into this Test and are only a wicket away from getting into the Proteas bowlers. Meanwhile, the hosts who will be pondering how they lost two wickets in two overs before a break, will hope for a partnership between their skipper, Du Plessis and the debutant, Wiaan Mulder who is expected to walk in next. Another 100-odd runs and the hosts will consider themselves to be in a safe position. The match and the series is on the line, and one could cut the tension with a knife here. An engrossing final session in the offing, join us at 1500 local (1300 GMT) for the resumption!

The last ten minutes have just changed the way the game was looking. Two wickets, that of Hashim Amla and Quinton de Kock will have given Sri Lanka the much-needed boost before the Tea break. Shoulders were dropping and the game seemed to be going away from the Lankans as the partnership between Amla and du Plessis was budding along. Dhananjaya though got a wicket against the run of play and Lakmal got De Kock caught and bowled. This interesting match has gotten even more interesting with South Africa effectively 159/5.

OUT! Soft dismissal! Wicket right at the stroke of a break again. It was Elgar before Lunch and now de Kock before Tea. A slightly shorter in length delivery on middle and leg, de Kock looks to push at it with hard hands. The ball however, sticks in the surface and also bounces a touch extra. De Kock looks to check his shot but by then, the ball hits the higher portion of the bat and lobs back towards Lakmal. He stretches his hands out to the left and takes it. He throws it up in joy and de Kock stands there in disgust. South Africa's top scorer of the first innings makes minimal impact in this one. Two quick wickets and South Africa are effectively 159 for 5. Sri Lanka still in this as they walk back for TEA ON DAY 2!
Good length delivery on off, Quinton keeps it out.
Length delivery on off, de Kock plays it to third man.
Good length delivery on middle, de Kock pushes it to mid on.
A single to end a successful over for Lanka. It is short and outside off, the batter slaps it through covers and a run is taken.
Flighted ball on middle, de Kock prods forward and pushes it to mid on.
Tosses it up on off, de Kock keeps it out.
Quinton de Kock walks out to the middle.

OUT! Taken at slip this time! Amla is not as lucky as his partner as this time the ball goes into the hands of first slip. Also, the Lankans have learnt from their mistake in the last over and moved the slip fielder a little more finer and that has paid dividends. The straighter one from de Silva, it lands on off. Amla defends for the non-existent turn. It goes off the outside edge and low towards Mendis. He gets his hands down in time and takes it. Amla does not make his start count and another budding partnership comes to an end. Timely wicket for the visitors.
Floated on middle, du Plessis tucks it towards the leg side for a run.
Flighted delivery on off, du Plessis defends it out.
The final ball is bowled on the stumps, Faf works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off and another leave.
Finally gets bat to one but this too was outside off. Since it was short, Faf goes back and punches it through point for a couple.
Third leave in a row as another delivery is outside off.
Once again it is outside off, the batsman does not fiddle with it.
On a length and outside off, the batter does not play at it.
Suranga Lakmal replaces Fernando.
Flighted delivery on off, Amla keeps it out.
On middle, Amla defends it off the back foot.
Full on middle and leg, du Plessis drives it towards mid on for a run.
Flighted delivery on middle, the skipper nudges it to the leg side.
FOUR! Tossed up on off, du Plessis looks to defend but gets an outside edge. However, it goes fine of first slip towards third man for a boundary.
FOUR! Good shot. Short and outside off, du Plessis makes room and slaps it through covers for a boundary.
Outside off again, Amla shoulders his arms to this one.
Outside off, Amla shuffles across the line and leaves it alone.
Length delivery on middle, du Plessis tucks it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Bowls a bouncer, du Plessis does well to duck under it.
Full on middle, du Plessis drives it to mid on.
Length delivery on middle, Amla flicks it towards mid-wicket for a run.
Loopy delivery on middle, Amla flicks it towards mid-wicket for a single.
Flighted delivery on off, Hashim keeps it out.
Tossed up on middle, Amla looks to defend but gets an edge to the off side.
Flighted delivery on middle and leg, Amla pushes it towards short leg where it fell short of him. The fielder does well to stop it and saves runs for his team.
On middle, Hashim blocks it well.
Floated on off, Amla defends it off the back foot.
Works it with the angle towards deep square leg for a single.
On the shorter side again, this is pushed down to mid off for a run.
Second leave in a row as it is once again outside off.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Easy again for du Plessis! On the pads, it is flicked through mid-wicket for a couple.
On the stumps, Faf pushes it to mid on.
On middle again, Amla blocks it well. Good start by Dhananjaya de Silva. Just 2 runs came from the over.
Tossed up on middle and leg, du Plessis drives it towards mid on for a run.
On middle, du Plessis pushes it to mid-wicket.
On middle, the skipper pushes it off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on middle, Amla drives it towards mid on for a run.
Tossed up on middle, Amla flicks it to mid-wicket.
Dhananjaya de Silva is into the attack.
A little too straight this one and Amla works it to fine leg for a single.
On the pads, Faf looks to flick but misses. It hits his thigh pad and rolls towards square leg for a run. Leg bye given.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
On the off stump and it is defended.
On the pads, it is tucked around the corner for an easy run.
Angles it away from the off pole, left alone.
Drags his length back but the line is the same. Blocked.
Fullish and on off, Faf du Plessis strokes it to mid off. He looks positive here.
On the off pole this time, du Plessis has to play at it and he does so with a forward defense.
Another one outside off, another leave.
Good length and outside the off pole, left alone.
FOUR! Faf is dealing boundaries here! Another easy ball to him. On the pads, he flicks it through mid-wicket and the ball races away.
Length delivery on middle, Faf flicks it towards square leg for a run. Big over for South Africa. 10 runs came from it.
FOUR! Second boundary of the over. Cracking cover drive from the captain. Full and outside off, du Plessis drives it beautifully through covers for a boundary.
Good length delivery on off, du Plessis keeps it out.
FOUR! Nice shot from the skipper. Full toss outside off, du Plessis drives it through covers for a boundary.
Length delivery on off, Amla pushes it towards third man for a run.
Good length delivery on off, Amla defends it off the front foot.
Faf Du Plessis makes his way out at number 5.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Once again Bavuma plays at a ball which he could have left and that brings about his downfall. Once again, nothing great about the delivery. It is on a length and in the 5th stump channel. Now if Bavuma stands normally, he will probably be leaving that ball but due to his shuffle, he ends up standing on off when he plays the ball. Hence, he goes after this one, ends up playing inside the line. The ball takes the outside edge and goes to the right of Dickwella. He takes it with a dive. Another failure for Bavuma and with regular wickets, Sri Lanka are managing to stay in the game. South Africa are 119 for 3 effectively.
Goes fuller this time and Bavuma strokes it back to the bowler.

Top shot! Does not go to the boundary but fetches three. Short and a little bit of width on offer. Amla rocks back quickly and then punches it through wide mid off. Perera there hares after it and keeps it in play just before it crosses the ropes. 50 up.
Once again hits the length and bowls it on off, Amla easily keeps it out.
Outside the off pole, Amla does not play at it.
On the off pole, Amla lunges and keeps it out.

DRINKS! It has been a good passage of play for both the teams. Sri Lanka did get the early wicket of Aiden Markram but Hashim Amla and Temba Bavuma have steadied the ship. The visitors will look to get two to three wickets quickly and put pressure on the hosts.
Length delivery on leg, Bavuma flicks it to the leg side.
On off, Bavuma defends it off the back foot.
Good length delivery on middle, Bavuma looks to defend but gets it of the inner half of the bat. It goes to square leg.
Full outside off, Bavuma drives it to mid off.
Length delivery on middle, Amla flicks it towards square leg for a run.
Outside off, Amla shoulders his arms to this one.
Full on off, Temba drives it to covers.
Good length delivery on off, Bavuma looks to leave the ball but gets hit on the pads.
Outside off, Temba covers the line of the stumps and lets it go.
Full on middle and leg, Bavuma drives it to mid on.
Good length delivery outside off, Bavuma shoulders his arms to this one.

Full on middle, Bavuma drives it back towards the bowler where Rajitha stops it with his outstretched right foot. It hits his the boot and goes towards mid on. Good fielding from the bowler, preventing runs.

In the air... dropped! Or is it? If it is, that is an absolute dolly. Karunaratne, the skipper, will be the culprit. Fernando's introduction back into the attack almost worked. Good change in length there. Fernando bends his back on this one and bowls it short. Amla is hurried into the pull, it seems to have hit his glove and lobbed towards first slip. DK there backtracks, gets two hands to it but fails to hang on. Now the reaction of the bowler shows that it was a chance. The replays have still not been shown.
On the shorter side and angling across the batsman, Amla shoulders arms to this one.
On the off pole this time, Amla plays it very late as he defends it onto the ground.
Outside off, looking to get the ball back in. No swing though and Amla shoulders arms to it.
On the off pole, Bavuma plays outside the line, it goes off the inner half towards mid-wicket for a single.
On the shorter side but it bounces up to a comfortable height for the batsman. Amla goes back and pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
Vishwa Fernando is back on.
Good running! Amla drops it towards point and scampers across to the other end. The fielder does have a shy at the non-striker's end but misses.
Outside off, left alone.
Just behind the driving length, Amla looks to drive but then the length wasn't there. He checks his shot and it goes to the man at covers.
On the off pole, Amla easily defends it.
On the shorter side, Bavuma cracks it through point. There is a fielder in the deep, a single is taken.

Lovely bowling! But Bavuma probably could have left that. Slightly outside off, Bavuma now due to his initial movement, is standing on off. He then looks to defend but gets beaten as he plays inside the line. The bowler puts in an appeal but he is the only one doing so.
Bowls it on the pads, Bavuma flicks it to deep square leg and retains strike. The partnership is 11 between the two, the lead is 111.
Goes back to bowling length but the line is outside off, Bavuma shoulders arms.
Goes short but at Lakmal's pace it is too easy for Amla to go back, pull it to deep square leg and cross ends.
Fuller in length, Amla drives it nicely but can't get it past mid off. No movement for Lakmal, even on the fuller deliveries.
On the off stump, Amla goes back and blocks it out.
Works it with the angle to wide mid on for a quick run.
Once again a little confusion! Full and on off, Amla strokes it towards mid off. It is to his right. The batsmen think of a run but then at the right time opt against it.
Another solid stroke but to the man at covers.
This time he plays it with a straight face and times it to mid off.
FOUR! Edgy but Amla won't mind! It looked a little deliberate though. Outside off, Amla plays it with soft hands and also an angled face. It takes the outside edge and races to the third man fence.
Leading edge but a run! Starts on the leg stump and then seams away a little. Bavuma looks to flick but it goes off the leading edge towards deep point for a single.
Outside off, Bavuma shuffles across and makes an easy leave.
Goes wide off the crease and slants it in on off, Amla with the angle defends it to mid-wicket. Maiden.
Gets it to rise from a length around off, Amla looks to defend but the ball hits the sticker.
Angles it into the batsman, Amla confidently strokes it to mid on.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Amla leaves at the last moment.
Back of a length on off, Amla gets right behind the line and defends it.
On the off stump, the batsman keeps it out.
Slight hesitation there. Bavuma strokes it towards the bowler, he makes a half-stop. The ball deflects towards mid off. TB thinks of a run but then is sent back.
In the 5th stump channel, left alone.
Once again the line is too straight, it is worked to mid on.
Attacks the off pole, Bavuma blocks it out. This is the length and the line Rajitha should be bowling.
Nicely driven! This is through cover-point. There is a fielder in the deep and it results only a single.
A little too straight, this is worked to fine leg for an easy run.
Good length delivery on off, Hashim defends it off the back foot.
On off, Amla defends it out.
Length delivery on off, Amla plays it to point.
Good length delivery again on off, Amla keeps it out.
Good length delivery on middle, Amla defends it off the back foot.
Length delivery on off, Bavuma drives it through covers. The batsmen pick up a couple. Bavuma is off the mark straightaway. The hosts' lead is over 100 now!
Temba Bavuma walks in at number 4, will be careful about his running this time hopefully...

OUT! What a catch that is! Markram stands there in disbelief and then slowly turns back and starts walking to the pavilion. Rajitha strikes in his first over but all credit has to be given to the fielder here. Not a great delivery, it was one which batsmen love. Full and on the pads, Markram senses an opportunity to hit it for a boundary. He flicks it right off the middle, he does not keep it down though. It is still a little away from the fielder. Oshada Fernando, however, dives full stretch to his right and takes it. A much-needed breakthrough as Markram seemed to be getting into his zone.
Another one which is angled into the off stump, Markram defends it right off the middle.
On the off pole, Markram gets right behind the line and keeps it out.
Outside off this time, it has been left alone.
Down the leg side, Markram looks to flick but misses. Would have been a wide in an ODI but not in Tests.

FOUR! Expansive but that was there to be hit. Short and width on offer, Markram transfers his weight on the back foot and punches it over covers for a boundary. Welcome into the attack Rajitha. Lead is one short of 100.
Kasun Rajitha is on now.
Outside off, Amla shoulders his arms to this one.
Length delivery on middle and leg, Markram flicks it towards square leg for a run.

Good length delivery on off, Markram plays it back towards the bowler. Lakmal tries to stop it but it goes through him. It hits the stumps at his end and goes towards mid-wicket. But no run for South Africa.
FOUR! Nice punch from Aiden. Short and outside off, Markram cuts it through point for a boundary.
Good length delivery on middle, Markram keeps it out.
On a good length on off, Markram defends it off the back foot.
Good length delivery on leg, Amla defends it off the back foot.
Length delivery on middle, Amla pushes it to the leg side.

We are back after Lunch. The players and umpires are out in the middle. Aiden Markram is out there and Hashim Amla will join him in the middle. Amla will face the first ball of this session by Vishwa Fernando as he will finish off what remains of his over.
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

South Africa on the other hand, need a couple of good sessions and one would probably believe they would bat the Lankans out of the game as the lead then would be above the 250-run mark. They still have a lot of batting to come and they would hope each and every batter who bats can contribute. Join us for the second session in a while.

South Africa do not enter Lunch unscathed. Exactly what Sri Lanka would have wanted in the little time they had before the break. Majority of the first session though did not belong to them. A poor batting display saw them concede a decent lead. However, they head into the break with momentum on their side and they would hope they can carry it forward in the post-Lunch session.

OUT! Fernando strikes! Sri Lanka get a wicket right at the stroke of Lunch. Again. What is with the hurry to eat food for the Saffas? Yesterday it was Faf. Today, it was Elgar. Good length delivery outside off, Dean looks to defend but ends up playing inside the line and gets an outside edge. The reason for the edge is that there was hardly any foot movement from DE. He had to reach out to that and seemed to be more worried about the ball coming in. That indecision costs him. The edge goes towards Dickwella who takes a comfortable catch. Nice end to the session for Sri Lanka who have had a forgetful morning. LUNCH ON DAY 2, SOUTH AFRICA ARE EFFECTIVELY 78/1!
